revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Locker Clue
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Ruiz finds a clue at a crime scene: 'A number of suspect's stolen coins, plus 7 more coins found in a locker, equals 31 coins in all.' Let c stand for the number of stolen coins. Write an equation that represents this clue, then find how many coins were stolen.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Equation: c + 7 = 31. Since c = 31 − 7 = 24, the suspect stole 24 coins.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do I turn a word clue into an equation?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: An equation says two amounts are equal. A value is a SOLUTION when substituting it makes that statement true — so any guess can be checked, not just solved for — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

onLevel.stem: A detective found some fingerprints on Monday and 14 more on Tuesday, for a total of 30. Which equation represents this?
onLevel.explanation: The detective's Monday fingerprints (f) plus 14 more equals 30: f + 14 = 30.
choiceFeedback: The 14 were found in addition to Monday's, so they are added, not subtracted.
Multiplying would mean the Monday prints were repeated 14 times over. The words say 14 more prints were found, which is about combining amounts.
Dividing splits the prints into 14 equal groups, which is not what happened on Tuesday. Reread what the detective did with the 14 new prints.
hints: Monday's fingerprints are the unknown f. On Tuesday she found 14 MORE, and the two days together total 30.
'More' means the two amounts combine into one total. Combining to reach a total is addition, not multiplying or dividing.
Write it in story order: f (Monday) plus 14 (Tuesday) equals 30 (total). Which choice shows that sum?
onLevel.stemEs: Un detective encontró algunas huellas dactilares el lunes y 14 más el martes, para un total de 30. ¿Cuál ecuación representa esto?
onLevel.explanationEs: Las huellas del lunes (f) más 14 más es igual a 30: f + 14 = 30.
hintsEs: Las huellas del lunes son la incógnita f. El martes encontró 14 MÁS, y los dos días juntos suman 30.
'Más' significa que las dos cantidades se combinan en un total. Combinar para llegar a un total es suma, no multiplicación ni división.
Escríbelo en el orden de la historia: f (lunes) más 14 (martes) es igual a 30 (total). ¿Qué opción muestra esa suma?

onLevel.title: Crack the Equation Error

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: A number of case files divided by 3 equals 6.
workedExample.workEs: Un número de expedientes dividido entre 3 es igual a 6.

workedExample.label: Choose a variable
workedExample.work: Let n be the number of case files.
workedExample.workEs: Sea n el número de expedientes.

onLevel.correctWork: 'Divided by 3' means division, not multiplication. The correct equation is n / 3 = 6, not 3n = 6. Check: 18 / 3 = 6.
hints: Does 'divided by 3' tell you to multiply by 3 or split into 3 equal groups?
'A number divided by 3' is n / 3, so the equation is n / 3 = 6.
onLevel.titleEs: Descifra el error de la ecuación
onLevel.explanation: The clue says the case files are divided by 3, but the equation 3n = 6 multiplies instead. Dividing means splitting n into 3 equal groups, so the equation is n / 3 = 6, and 18 / 3 = 6 confirms it.
onLevel.explanationEs: La pista dice que los expedientes se dividen entre 3, pero la ecuación 3n = 6 multiplica en su lugar. Dividir significa repartir n en 3 grupos iguales, así que la ecuación es n / 3 = 6, y 18 / 3 = 6 lo confirma.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 'Dividido entre 3' significa división, no multiplicación. La ecuación correcta es n / 3 = 6, no 3n = 6. Comprueba: 18 / 3 = 6.
hintsEs: ¿'Dividido entre 3' te dice que multipliques por 3 o que repartas en 3 grupos iguales?
'Un número dividido entre 3' es n / 3, así que la ecuación es n / 3 = 6.

onLevel.title: Find the Equation Error

workedExample.label: Situation
workedExample.workEs: El doble de un número es 16

onLevel.correctWork: 'Twice' means multiply by 2, not add 2. The correct equation is 2n = 16.
hints: What does 'twice' really mean — adding or multiplying?
'Twice a number' means 2 times the number, so the equation is 2n = 16.
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la ecuación
onLevel.explanation: The operation was named wrong at the start: 'twice' was called addition, which led to n + 2 = 16. Twice a number means two of that number, which is multiplication, so the equation is 2n = 16.
onLevel.explanationEs: La operación se nombró mal desde el inicio: se dijo que 'twice' era una suma, lo que llevó a n + 2 = 16. El doble de un número significa dos veces ese número, que es multiplicación, así que la ecuación es 2n = 16.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 'El doble' significa multiplicar por 2, no sumar 2. La ecuación correcta es 2n = 16.
hintsEs: ¿Qué significa realmente 'el doble' — sumar o multiplicar?
'El doble de un número' significa 2 por el número, así que la ecuación es 2n = 16.

onLevel.prompt: Write a real-world situation that can be modeled by the equation n / 5 = 9. Explain what n represents and verify your equation makes sense.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: Situation: ___. In this problem, n represents ___. Check: n = ___ because ___ ÷ 5 = 9.
onLevel.hint: Use a strategy or example from the lesson to help you explain your answer.
hints: n / 5 = 9 says: some amount n is split into 5 equal shares, and each share is 9. Think of things that get shared equally.
Pick a context — n stickers shared by 5 friends, n dollars split 5 ways. Say clearly what n counts, then check your value by multiplying 9 × 5.
Start your sentence: 'I had n ___ and split them equally among 5 ___; each got 9.' Then find n by computing 9 × 5 and checking it back.
onLevel.explanation: The equation n / 5 = 9 describes one amount being shared into 5 equal groups with 9 in each group, so a matching story could be n stickers split evenly among 5 friends with each friend getting 9. Since 5 groups of 9 rebuild the whole, n = 9 × 5 = 45, and 45 ÷ 5 = 9 checks the story.
onLevel.explanationEs: La ecuación n / 5 = 9 describe una cantidad que se reparte en 5 grupos iguales con 9 en cada grupo, así que una historia que encaja podría ser n calcomanías repartidas entre 5 amigos y cada uno recibe 9. Como 5 grupos de 9 reconstruyen el total, n = 9 × 5 = 45, y 45 ÷ 5 = 9 comprueba la historia.
onLevel.promptEs: Escribe una situación de la vida real que se pueda modelar con la ecuación n / 5 = 9. Explica qué representa n y comprueba que tu ecuación tiene sentido.
hintsEs: n / 5 = 9 dice: una cantidad n se reparte en 5 partes iguales y cada parte es 9. Piensa en cosas que se reparten por igual.
Escoge un contexto: n calcomanías repartidas entre 5 amigos, n dólares divididos en 5. Di claramente qué cuenta n y comprueba tu valor multiplicando 9 × 5.
Empieza tu oración: 'Tenía n ___ y los repartí en partes iguales entre 5 ___; a cada uno le tocaron 9.' Luego halla n calculando 9 × 5 y compruébalo.

extending.stem: A witness statement reads: 'A number c of security cameras plus 6 more equals 19.' Which equation matches?
extending.explanation: 'Plus 6 more' means + 6 and 'equals 19' means = 19, so c + 6 = 19. Check: 13 + 6 = 19.
choiceFeedback: Check the operation: "plus" means add, not multiply.
That shows removing 6. The words say plus 6.
The problem asks you to add, not divide.
extending.stemEs: Una declaración de un testigo dice: 'Un número c de cámaras de seguridad más 6 más es igual a 19.' ¿Cuál ecuación corresponde?
extending.explanationEs: 'Más 6 más' significa + 6 y 'es igual a 19' significa = 19, así que c + 6 = 19. Comprueba: 13 + 6 = 19.
hints: An equation matches the words piece by piece: a starting amount, an operation, and what the total equals.
Name the unknown first — c is the number of cameras you do not know yet — then translate 'plus 6 more' into an operation.
Begin writing it: c comes first, then the operation for 'plus 6 more', then the equals sign with 19. Pick the operation the words describe.
hintsEs: Una ecuación corresponde a las palabras parte por parte: una cantidad inicial, una operación y a cuánto es igual el total.
Nombra primero la incógnita: c es el número de cámaras que aún no conoces. Luego traduce 'más 6 más' a una operación.
Empieza a escribirla: primero va c, luego la operación de 'más 6 más', y después el signo igual con 19. Elige la operación que describen las palabras.

extending.stem: The lab tech says: '5 times the number of evidence bags b equals 35.' Which equation represents this clue?
extending.explanation: '5 times the number' means 5 times b, so 5b = 35. Check: 5 × 7 = 35.
choiceFeedback: "Times" means multiply, not add.
That shows subtracting 5. The words say 5 times.
"Times" means multiply, not divide.
extending.stemEs: El técnico del laboratorio dice: '5 veces el número de bolsas de evidencia b es igual a 35.' ¿Cuál ecuación representa esta pista?
extending.explanationEs: '5 veces el número' significa 5 por b, así que 5b = 35. Comprueba: 5 × 7 = 35.
hints: Words like 'times' tell you exactly which operation belongs in the equation.
The unknown is b, the number of evidence bags, and the clue says that amount is repeated a certain number of times.
'5 times b' is written by putting the 5 directly in front of b. Set that expression equal to 35 and see which choice matches.
hintsEs: Palabras como 'veces' te dicen exactamente qué operación va en la ecuación.
La incógnita es b, el número de bolsas de evidencia, y la pista dice que esa cantidad se repite cierto número de veces.
'5 veces b' se escribe poniendo el 5 justo delante de b. Iguala esa expresión a 35 y observa cuál opción coincide.

extending.stem: A torn note reads: 'A suspect's case minutes m, after 9 fewer, leaves 24.' Which equation fits?
extending.explanation: '9 fewer' means subtract 9, so m − 9 = 24. Check: 33 − 9 = 24.
choiceFeedback: The clue says "fewer" or "less" — use subtraction, not addition.
Subtraction is needed here, not multiplication.
Use subtraction for "fewer" or "less," not division.
extending.stemEs: Una nota rota dice: 'Los minutos m del caso de un sospechoso, después de 9 menos, dejan 24.' ¿Cuál ecuación corresponde?
extending.explanationEs: '9 menos' significa restar 9, así que m − 9 = 24. Comprueba: 33 − 9 = 24.
hints: Read the words in the order the amount changes: something started, something was taken away, and something was left.
'9 fewer' means 9 are removed from the starting amount m, not the other way around.
Start with m, then take away the 9 that were lost, and set the result equal to what remains.
hintsEs: Lee las palabras en el orden en que cambia la cantidad: algo empezó, algo se quitó y algo quedó.
'9 menos' significa que se quitan 9 de la cantidad inicial m, no al revés.
Empieza con m, quita los 9 que se perdieron e iguala el resultado a lo que queda.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — Crack the Detective's Mistake

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: A number of footprints divided by 4 equals 6.
workedExample.workEs: Un número de huellas dividido entre 4 es igual a 6.

workedExample.label: Choose a variable
workedExample.work: Let f represent the number of footprints.
workedExample.workEs: Sea f el número de huellas.

extending.correctWork: 'Divided by 4' means division, not multiplication. The correct equation is f / 4 = 6. Check: 24 / 4 = 6.
hints: Reread the clue: does 'divided by 4' mean you multiply by 4 or split into 4?
'Divided by 4' is f / 4, so the equation is f / 4 = 6, not 4f = 6.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Descifra el error del detective
extending.explanation: Choosing f for the footprints was fine, but the equation 4f = 6 turns the division into a multiplication. 'Divided by 4' means f is split into 4 equal groups, so the equation is f / 4 = 6, and 24 / 4 = 6 confirms it.
extending.explanationEs: Elegir f para las huellas estuvo bien, pero la ecuación 4f = 6 convierte la división en una multiplicación. 'Dividido entre 4' significa que f se reparte en 4 grupos iguales, así que la ecuación es f / 4 = 6, y 24 / 4 = 6 lo confirma.
extending.correctWorkEs: 'Dividido entre 4' significa división, no multiplicación. La ecuación correcta es f / 4 = 6. Comprueba: 24 / 4 = 6.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pista: ¿'dividido entre 4' significa multiplicar por 4 o repartir en 4?
'Dividido entre 4' es f / 4, así que la ecuación es f / 4 = 6, no 4f = 6.

extending.stem: Which equation represents: 'A number plus 12 equals 30'?
extending.explanation: 'Plus' means addition, so the equation is n + 12 = 30.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 'Plus' means addition, so the equation is n + 12 = ___.
Check the operation: "plus" means add, not multiply.
The problem asks you to add, not divide.
hints: Find the operation word in the sentence. What does 'plus' tell you to do with the number and 12?
Let n stand for the unknown number, then translate each phrase into symbols: 'a number' becomes n, 'plus 12' names an operation, 'equals 30' becomes = 30.
Build it left to right: n, then the symbol for 'plus', then 12, then '= 30'. Which choice matches that exact order?
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Un número más 12 es igual a 30'?
extending.explanationEs: 'Más' significa suma, así que la ecuación es n + 12 = 30.
hintsEs: Halla la palabra de operación en la oración. ¿Qué te dice 'más' que hagas con el número y el 12?
Deja que n represente el número desconocido y luego traduce cada frase a símbolos: 'un número' se vuelve n, 'más 12' nombra una operación y 'es igual a 30' se vuelve = 30.
Ármalo de izquierda a derecha: n, luego el símbolo de 'más', luego 12, luego '= 30'. ¿Qué opción coincide con ese orden exacto?

extending.stem: Which equation represents: 'Seven less than a number is 18'?
extending.explanation: 'Seven less than a number' means start with the number and subtract 7: n − 7 = 18.
choiceFeedback: Start with the variable, then subtract — not the other way.
The clue says "fewer" or "less" — use subtraction, not addition.
Use subtraction for "fewer" or "less," not division.
hints: 'Seven less than a number' is tricky — the number comes FIRST, and then 7 is taken away from it.
'Less than' flips the wording: '7 less than n' means start at n and subtract 7, not start at 7 and subtract n.
Write the number first: n, then subtract 7, then set it equal to 18. Which choice is built in that order?
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Siete menos que un número es 18'?
extending.explanationEs: 'Siete menos que un número' significa empezar con el número y restar 7: n − 7 = 18.
hintsEs: 'Siete menos que un número' es tramposo: el número va PRIMERO y luego se le quitan 7.
'Menos que' invierte el enunciado: '7 menos que n' significa empezar en n y restar 7, no empezar en 7 y restar n.
Escribe el número primero: n, luego resta 7 y luego iguálalo a 18. ¿Qué opción está armada en ese orden?

extending.stem: Which equation represents: 'Three times a number equals 21'?
extending.explanation: 'Three times' means multiply by 3, so the equation is 3n = 21.
choiceFeedback: "Times" means multiply, not add.
That shows subtracting 3. The words say three times.
"Times" means multiply, not divide.
hints: Circle the operation word: 'times'. What operation does 'times' always signal?
'Three times a number' means 3 multiplied by n, written 3n with no symbol between the 3 and the n.
Put 3n on the left and set it equal to 21. Which choice shows multiplication instead of adding or subtracting 3?
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Tres veces un número es igual a 21'?
extending.explanationEs: 'Tres veces' significa multiplicar por 3, así que la ecuación es 3n = 21.
hintsEs: Encierra la palabra de operación: 'veces'. ¿Qué operación señala siempre 'veces'?
'Tres veces un número' significa 3 multiplicado por n, y se escribe 3n sin ningún símbolo entre el 3 y la n.
Pon 3n a la izquierda e iguálalo a 21. ¿Qué opción muestra multiplicación en vez de sumar o restar 3?

extending.stem: Is n = 3 a solution of n + 5 = 9?
choices: No, because 3 + 5 = 8, which does not equal 9
You cannot tell without solving first
extending.explanation: Substitute the value and check whether the statement is true: 3 + 5 = 8, and 8 ≠ 9, so 3 is not a solution.
choiceFeedback: Being smaller than 9 does not make a value a solution.
An equation is true or false — close does not count.
Substituting is exactly how you check a value without solving.
hints: Replace n with 3.
Work out the left side.
Does it equal the right side?
extending.explanationEs: Sustituye el valor y revisa si el enunciado es verdadero: 3 + 5 = 8, y 8 ≠ 9, así que 3 no es una solución.
choicesEs: No, porque 3 + 5 = 8, que no es igual a 9
No se puede saber sin resolver primero
hintsEs: Reemplaza n por 3.
Resuelve el lado izquierdo.
¿Es igual al lado derecho?

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Write Equations is writing subtraction and division clues in the wrong order — putting the number from the clue first instead of the variable first. For 'a number decreased by 8 equals 5,' students often write 8 − n = 5 instead of the correct n − 8 = 5; for 'a number divided by 4 equals 6,' they write 4 ÷ n (or 4n) instead of n / 4 = 6. Always start with the variable, then attach the operation in the order the words describe it, and check by substituting your answer back in.

diagram.title: Stolen Paintings Part-Whole
diagram.caption: The whole bar is all 37 stolen paintings; it splits into recovered (p) and 14 still missing, so p + 14 = 37 gives p = 23.

connect.scenario: A detective is tracking stolen paintings. She knows that the number of paintings recovered plus 14 paintings still missing equals the 37 total stolen. The equation p + 14 = 37 represents this situation.
connect.promptQuestion: How many paintings has the detective recovered? How did writing an equation help you understand the situation?
connect.prompt: The detective recovered ___ paintings because p + 14 = 37 means p = 37 − ___ = ___.

choices: To keep the equation balanced while isolating p
Because subtraction is easier than addition
To make the answer a whole number
check.explanation: An equation is a balance. Whatever you do to one side you must do to the other, or the two sides stop being equal.
Substituting p = 23 back in gives 23 + 14 = 37, which is true. That confirms the solution.

connect.modelAnswer: p + 14 = 37. Subtract 14 from both sides: p = 37 − 14 = 23 paintings recovered. Check it: 23 + 14 = 37. ✓

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — Which value is the solution of n + 5 = 9, and how do you know?
choices: n = 5, because 5 appears in the equation
exitTicket.explanation: Substitute each value and check. Replacing n with 4 gives 4 + 5 = 9, a true statement, so 4 is the solution.
choiceFeedback: That adds the two numbers shown instead of finding what joins with 5 to make 9.
An equation is either true or false when a value is substituted — close does not make it a solution.
A number appearing in the equation is not automatically its solution; substitute and check.
